problem_statement: The paper frames the problem as protecting critical financial infrastructure from advanced cyber threats, including advanced persistent threats, data breaches, and sophisticated DeFi fraud. It also treats financial risk management as needing secure, transparent, and real-time detection and monitoring.
problem_statement_quotes:
The rising sophistication of cyber threats
targeting critical financial infrastructure necessitates
a paradigm shift in risk management and cyberse-
curity defenses.

Critical financial infrastructure faces unmatched
threats from advanced persistent threats (APTs) and
sophisticated DeFi fraud schemes [1], [3].

This paper presents Q-DTN, a novel framework
integrating Quantum Machine Learning (QML) with
Decentralized Trust Networks (DTNs) to deliver se-
cure, transparent, and efficient financial risk man-
agement, leveraging quantum computing’s exponen-
tial speedups [17] and blockchain’s decentralized
security [7].
classical_baseline: The paper compares against traditional risk management models such as Value at Risk and against classical AI approaches, including XGBoost and neural networks. It also references standalone QSVMs as a stronger classical-style benchmark in the related-work discussion and experiments.
classical_baseline_quotes:
Traditional risk management models like Value at Risk (VaR) as-
sume stable markets and struggle with intricate, high-
speed data [20]. Classical AI approaches encounter
computational limits and centralized vulnerabilities
[15], exposing systems to systemic risks [6].
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical risk models struggle with high-speed, intricate data, and that classical AI has computational limits and centralized vulnerabilities. It also states that the target threats can be computationally intractable for classical models because of the curse of dimensionality.
classical_difficulty_quotes:
Traditional risk management models like Value at Risk (VaR) as-

speed data [20]. Classical AI approaches encounter

This quantum-native transfor-
mation enables the identification of complex, non-
linear correlations indicative of sophisticated finan-
cial threats—such as advanced persistent threats or
synthetic identity fraud—that are computationally
intractable for classical models due to the curse

business_stakes: The paper emphasizes real-world stakes around regulatory compliance, data exposure, and production use in banking, fintech, and critical infrastructure protection. It also highlights the need for low overhead and real-time monitoring.
business_stakes_quotes:
An Explainable Quantum AI (XQAI) module
ensures compliance.

The DTN utilizes smart contracts and zero-knowledge
proofs (zk-SNARKs) to facilitate secure, privacy-
preserving threat intelligence sharing among partic-
ipating financial institutions without exposing sen-
sitive transaction data.

Q-DTN achieves 97% accuracy and 0.95 F1-
Score with 10s training time, outperforming classical
benchmarks by 50x speedup.

The framework’s 97% accuracy with zero data
exposure establishes a new benchmark for quantum-
secured financial risk management systems. The in-
tegration of quantum computing with decentralized
trust networks establishes a new paradigm for critical
infrastructure protection, with immediate applica-
tions in banking, fintech, and regulatory compliance
systems.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is strongly framed around financial cybersecurity/fraud and risk management.
